title: One Table, Two Names
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mediterranean Travels
description: Hover over and click six pairs of dishes on one table, Turkish above and Greek below, to learn both names and what the two kitchens share, then test yourself in Quiz mode.

learningObjectives: The learner will match six Turkish and Greek dish pairs, give both names for each, and explain, without taking a side, why the two kitchens share so many dishes: one empire for centuries, and the population exchange of 1923.
prerequisites: Meze, coffee, and baklava, from [Chapter 6](../../chapters/06-bazaars-scripts-presses/index.md), and the population exchange, from [Chapter 7](../../chapters/07-end-of-empire-modern-turkey/index.md).

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Side-by-side comparison followed by retrieval practice
keyQuestions: What do the two kitchens share, and why?
What does each pair differ in?
commonMisconceptions: One country invented every shared dish.
A shared dish means a shared name.
assessmentOpportunities: Quiz mode: click the zone that matches each idea

controls.name: Explore
controls.description: Default mode: hover a zone for a tooltip, click it for the infobox.

controls.name: Quiz Mode
controls.description: Hides the name pills and asks 10 questions answered by clicking a zone.
